messages:
Maya: FYI — customer Acorn reported a big p95/p99 regression after a scale event ~2026-03-12 11:12 UTC. They see 500s and long tails. ticket #AC-2419.
Jordan: Got it. Any request IDs or example timestamps?
Maya: Sent sample req IDs in the ticket: req=ac-4f7a, ac-4f7b, ac-4f7c. Stack traces show attach timeouts and a couple 401s.
Kevin: Repro steps from customer: heavy traffic at 11:10, failed calls, then retries. They say "requests wait 6-15s before 500".
Sam: ops-bot alert fired for attach_latency_p99 > 8s at 11:13.
ops-bot: alert: attach_latency_p99=12.1s (threshold=8s) svc=dedicated-pool-priority region=us-west2
Jordan: Can someone grab inference node logs + attach service logs around 11:10-11:20? Start with `rg "attach" logs | sed -n '1,200p'` and `kubectl -n infra logs svc/attach-router --since=20m`.
Kevin: Pasting a small log snippet from Acorn customer trace:```
[11:12:02] attach request id=ac-4f7a pool=priority attach_start
[11:12:03] auth: token validation failed tenant=acorn error=401
[11:12:03] attach router: fallback to default-pool for req=ac-4f7a
[11:12:08] provisioner: provision VM start vm=ded-42
[11:12:14] vm attach timeout req=ac-4f7a error=attach_timeout
```
Sam: 401s + fallbacks makes sense — if auth fails, requests get routed away -> retries -> fanout to other pools -> storm. Any recent auth changes deployed?
Maya: Deploy-bot shows auth-service rollout at 11:09 (canary then full).
deploy-bot: rollout auth-service v2.8.3 -> v2.9.0 finished at 11:11 (canary success).
Jordan: Hmm possible key rotation or a transient bug in token validation. If some tokens were rejected temporarily, many clients retried and hit dedicated pools concurrently causing saturation and cold GPU starts.
Kevin: Customer logs show 401s only for a subset of tokens (they rotate tokens every 6h). Maybe new auth validator read stale key during canary window.
Sam: Action items: 1) Confirm auth validator key sync across instances. 2) Short-term mitigation: raise minpool for Acorn priority pool and enable prewarm for priority queue. 3) Add randomized attach backoff for retries. 4) Rate-limit per-customer attach-fanout while we stabilize.
Jordan: I can run a quick query: `select count(*) from attach_events where tenant='acorn' and ts between '11:10' and '11:20'` — results: 18k attach attempts, baseline is ~1.2k. Fanout x15.
Sam: Oof. Run infra-cli to bump minpool: `infra-cli pools set-min acorn-priority --min 4 --region us-west2` — this will buy headroom. Also enable prewarm: `infra-cli pools set-prewarm acorn-priority --count 2`.
ops-bot: executing: infra-cli pools set-min ...
ops-bot: completed: min=4 prewarm=2 for acorn-priority (applied by Sam)
Jordan: I'll push a temporary per-tenant attach rate limit: `gateway set-rate-limit --tenant acorn --attach 30/s` to limit new attach churn.
ops-bot: rate-limit applied tenant=acorn attach=30/s (by Jordan)
Kevin: Also toggled attach retry jitter to randomized exponential (0 - 600ms) in gateway config to avoid synchronized retry storms.
Sam: Checking consumer-facing errors: after changes p95 dropped from ~8.5s to ~1.1s within 3 minutes. p99 at ~2.6s.
Maya: Customer confirmed fewer 500s and said throughput restored ~11:17.
Jordan: Root cause hypothesis: auth-service canary rolled a validator with race in key-sync that caused intermittent 401s for rotating tokens. That triggered client retry fanout into dedicated pools causing cold GPU provisioning and attach timeouts.
Kevin: Next steps for next 24h: 1) Revert to stable validator while we patch key-sync. 2) Improve canary gating to monitor auth 401 spikes tied to token rotation metadata. 3) Add automatic prewarm when per-tenant attach rate > threshold. 4) Postmortem and customer follow-up.
Sam: I've reverted canary to v2.8.3 while engineering prepares a patch. deploy-bot: rollback auth-service -> v2.8.3 completed at 11:28.
Maya: I'll update ticket #AC-2419 with timeline, mitigations, and customer remediation steps (token refresh guidance).
Jordan: We should add an alert that correlates auth-401 spike + attach_fallbacks so future incidents triage faster.
Kevin: Agreed. I'll create the alert PR after breakfast.
Maya: Thanks team. Closing loop with customer now. :thumbsup:
